cf:artificer-infusions.wants: a shared per-encounter allowance of more than one use -- group= counts to one -- and chargen.power_choice() for the card the page offers in place of another
cf:artificer-infusions.why: the fourth feature is the budget the three declared infusion rows draw on: two per extended rest, one per round, three from 16th level. Each row is written as its own encounter power with once_per_round, which is three separate allowances rather than one shared one. The second half was filed as chargen.BUILDS and that was the wrong symbol: a Build records which secondary a fork leans on and carries no card list, so a leg could not express one card taken in place of another

cf:artificer-items.wants: magic items in the engine: an item with a daily power, Gear recording what is worn or carried, and an event announcing that an item's daily power was used
cf:artificer-items.why: three of the artificer's four class-page features are about magic items and none of the three has a subject. One banks a charge in a weapon or implement that its wielder spends for a bonus to an attack roll already made; one recharges an item's daily power; one pays an ally temporary hit points whenever that ally uses an item's daily power. Gear carries weapons and armour and no items at all, every chassis weapon has enhancement 0, and nothing anywhere uses an item power, so each of the three would be a hook nothing ever fires

cf:assassin-training-guild.wants: c.no_encounter_attacks(), or a c.forbid that takes a class-and-usage set rather than one ref
cf:assassin-training-guild.why: the second of the two printed methods is a granted row -- p14372, which chargen.loadout already deals -- plus the loss of every encounter attack power in the class. The grant half is written as a c.forbid on the other leg; the loss half would be a hand-listed set of refs that goes stale the moment a level is added, and a half-written version would leave an assassin holding the encounter powers its method says it never learned

cf:barbarian-might-rest.wants: the cf:barbarian-f1s0 row, which is the one option of the four nobody has declared
cf:barbarian-might-rest.why: filed when the compendium carried only the first option's text and the class had two derived legs. Both are fixed: class_feature carries cf:barbarian-f1s0 .. f1s3 and chargen.BUILDS["barbarian"] has five named legs that 23 riders ask about. Three of the four sub-option rows are written in features/primal_shadow.py; the fourth is named by a feat as todo=("cf:barbarian-f1s0",) and has no declaration

cf:druid-at-wills.wants: a per-class at-will count in chargen.SLOTS, and a composition rule chargen.loadout can honour
cf:druid-at-wills.why: the class's first printed feature is that a druid begins with three at-will attack powers and that at least one of them, and no more than two, must have the beast form keyword. SLOTS is two at-wills for every class in the game, and loadout picks them by the build's primary ability with no notion of a required keyword -- so the druid it deals has two at-wills and neither is a beast form row, which leaves the class's other feature, the shape change, leading nowhere. Nothing recorded it: the shape change is declared, so the class read as finished

cf:fighter-opening-stop.wants: c.halt(on=), plus movement.walk asking whether the mover may still move between steps rather than only before the first one
cf:fighter-opening-stop.why: the card is imported now and its second sentence is a real clause -- an enemy hit by the opportunity attack stops moving, if a move provoked it -- but the window opens inside walk's loop and step never re-asks can_move, so immobilising the mover there leaves it walking the rest of its path

cf:fighter-talent-rest.wants: a hand key in the attack context (the p7399 gap), Gear recording a free/empty off hand, an armour field on chargen.Build, and improvised weapons
cf:fighter-talent-rest.why: three of the six talents are left: one turns on wielding an off-hand weapon, one on an empty off hand, and one on improvised weapons and on not wearing heavy armour -- the chassis wears scale and Build cannot say otherwise, so each would be a gate that is false for every fighter in the tree

cf:invoker-covenant-channel.wants: something that says which covenant grants which of the two channelled rows -- the covenant named in each row's own spec, or a build column on class_feature filled in for this class
cf:invoker-covenant-channel.why: each covenant hands over one channel divinity power and the tree has both, p5186 and p7150, dealt to every invoker by loadout. cf:invoker-f1 writes the manifestation half, which the page prints in full for both covenants, but the specs are sanitised: neither row says what it is called and neither covenant's clause says what its power does. Forbidding the wrong one would take a working row off the board to express half a sentence

cf:monk-discipline.wants: a per-round sibling of the group= header field, plus the full discipline keyword declared on the rows that print it
cf:monk-discipline.why: the printed rule is one such power per round across a set of rows, and group= is the only cross-row budget the engine has -- it is per encounter, which is a different sentence. Nothing marks which rows are in the set either, so the budget would have no members to count

cf:rogue-melee-talent-die.wants: a thrown light blade in chargen, plus c.step_die() -- a modifier that moves a weapon's damage die one size
cf:rogue-melee-talent-die.why: the card's first sentence raises the die of a weapon no chassis carries, and nothing in the modifier language steps a die at all, so both halves of the clause are missing rather than one

cf:runepriest-rune-switch.wants: Keyword.RUNIC declared on the rows whose type line prints it, plus a rune offered when one of them is used and a state the choice writes
cf:runepriest-rune-switch.why: the class's first feature is a pair of states and the rule for entering one: the rune is chosen as part of using a runic power, and the state stands until another is chosen or the encounter ends. cf:runepriest-f0 writes the state and both of its standing benefits, chosen once as the fight begins, because nothing marks a row as runic -- Keyword has no member for it and group= is a per-encounter budget rather than a keyword -- so no row can announce a rune and there is no moment for the state to change at. The same gap as the rage keyword p4807 names

cf:runepriest-tradition-rest.wants: a Build field for armour, so a leg can wear something lighter than the class chassis
cf:runepriest-tradition-rest.why: the leg half is done: chargen.BUILDS["runepriest"] carries a leg per printed tradition and all three rows gate on their own, so cf:runepriest-f2s1 no longer shares a leg with cf:runepriest-f2s0. What is left is that tradition's armour clause -- it pays a Wisdom modifier to AC only out of heavy armour and the chassis wears scale, so the clause is written, asked live, and false in every fight. Build carries weapons and no armour, and the leg already carries the heavy blade the same sentence grants

cf:seeker-bond-rest.wants: the second bond's text on the imported class page
cf:seeker-bond-rest.why: the page prints one of the two bonds in full and cf:seeker-f1 writes all of it -- the granted row, the exclusivity, and the standing minor-action shift. The other bond is not in the imported text at all. Its granted row is identifiable without it, p11462 being the only other level-0 seeker row and the one that spends the Strength modifier its riders spend, so the exclusivity is written both ways; whatever else that bond gives is not on the page and is not guessed at

cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.wants: an event announcing a power use's finished effects (the p10354 gap), carrying the natural roll
cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.why: each source ends with a rider on a natural 20 -- and one of them a second on a natural 1 -- that lands after the attack's other effects. AttackRolled is the only event carrying the natural and it fires before the damage, so a slide-and-prone hung there would resolve in the wrong order, and Hit carries no natural at all

cf:sorcerer-soul-pierce.wants: c.ignore_resistance(dtype, up_to=), read by resolve.damage before Defences.resist is subtracted
cf:sorcerer-soul-pierce.why: both written halves of the sorcerer's source end with the same clause -- the caster's arcane powers ignore a target's resistance to the sworn type up to the value of the caster's own -- and resistance is subtracted from a flat number on the target with nothing on the attacker's side consulted, so the clause has nowhere to be read

cf:sorcerer-soul-rest.wants: a leg in chargen.BUILDS["sorcerer"] for the fourth source, carrying the three-phase cycle rather than one phase of it
cf:sorcerer-soul-rest.why: the page prints four sources. Three have a leg and are written. The fourth is a three-phase cycle chosen at the end of a short or an extended rest and stepped on by being bloodied or by spending a daily. **events.ShortRested is emitted now** -- turns.py:686, with ExtendedRested beside it, and features/sorcerer.py already listens -- so the moment the old wants asked for exists and this is no longer blocked on the engine. What is left is the leg: BUILDS has wild, dragon and the four elements, and a leg carrying one phase of three would deal a sorcerer a feature that never advances.

cf:warlord-archer.why: spec.py can read the class page now and the card is three clauses: it drops two proficiencies, adds one, and lets a ranged basic attack with a bow roll Strength for the attack and the damage. basic.RANGED fixes its ability in the header and nothing can rewrite it for one creature; a bow on a warlord leg in chargen.BUILDS is wanted too, because no leg carries one and there would be nothing to shoot with

cf:wizard-familiar.wants: something that puts a familiar on the board -- a Companion of kind "familiar" -- plus a leg in chargen.BUILDS["wizard"] for the second version of the class the page prints
cf:wizard-familiar.why: the class page carries a whole second set of features that nothing in the tree had a ref for, and both of its combat clauses hang on a familiar: a damage resistance for the wizard and its allies while adjacent to it, and a bonus feat whose only in-fight content is that the familiar exists at all. c.familiar and c.familiar_mode are built and four wizard rows already read them, but no row anywhere creates one, so every such call answers None and this feature would be a resistance nobody ever gets. The third feature of that set is four cantrips, which are declared and need nothing

cf:wizard-implement-rest.wants: legs in chargen.BUILDS["wizard"] for the three masteries with none, plus c.store_row(ref) for the one that banks an unprepared encounter power and a summon-time damage hook for the one that pays its summoned creatures
cf:wizard-implement-rest.why: the page's build sections name a class feature for two builds the tree has no leg for, and a third mastery no build names at all. Each of the three is a real clause -- bank a power, pay a summoning, repeat a missed illusion against a second target -- and none of the three has anything for c.build to answer, so adding a leg first would deal a wizard whose mastery does nothing. The docstring on cf:wizard-arcanist-f0 claimed this file already said so; it did not

p10275:augment1.wants: Effect.keywords, so c.save(against=) can name a charm or a fear effect rather than matching a label substring
p10275:augment1.why: the bonus applies only to a save against a charm or fear effect, and every effect's label is the ref of the row that laid it, so the gate would be false for every charm in the game

p11106:augment1.wants: c.must_attack(on=, against=) plus a way to say that enemies provoke from a creature
p11106:augment1.why: 'enemies provoke opportunity attacks from the target, and it must make those attacks' needs both halves; c.provoke opens one window for one named attacker and nothing obliges anybody to answer it

p11158:augment1.wants: c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause) -- a row that adds an offer to another row's augment
p11158:augment1.why: the aspect's whole content is an augmentation lent to the battlemind's at-will attacks while it stands; nothing hangs a clause on another row's augment, and the same shape is p11165, p11172, p13030 and p13043

p11165:augment1.wants: c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause) -- a row that adds an offer to another row's augment
p11165:augment1.why: an aspect daily whose Augment 1 is bought when some other at-will is augmented, not when this row is used

p11172:augment1.wants: c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause) -- a row that adds an offer to another row's augment
p11172:augment1.why: an aspect daily whose Augment 1 is bought when some other at-will is augmented, not when this row is used

p12422:augment2.wants: dsl.Range.by_ability, a reach sized off an ability modifier
p12422:augment2.why: Augment 1 -- reach + 1 -- is now written as dsl.Augment(reach=); Augment 2 is reach + Charisma modifier, and a Range holds a number read off the card before any creature is in hand

p12934:augment1.wants: c.revealed(on=) -- clearing Relation.HIDDEN_FROM from the creature being looked at
p12934:augment1.why: the clause strips concealment and invisibility; c.no_cover says the first and only c.see_invisible answers the second, and that sits on whoever is looking rather than on the target

p12947:augment2.wants: c.deals_half(when=) -- half damage narrowed to some of a creature's attacks
p12947:augment2.why: 'deals half damage with any attack that is not a basic attack' is Condition.WEAKENED, which query.deals_half reads off the creature rather than off the attack

p12958:augment1.wants: c.deals_half(when=) -- half damage narrowed to some of a creature's attacks
p12958:augment1.why: the same gate, on basic attacks this time; its Charisma modifier is not written alone

p13030:augment1.wants: c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause) -- a row that adds an offer to another row's augment
p13030:augment1.why: an aspect daily whose Augment 1 is bought when some other at-will is augmented, not when this row is used

p13043:augment1.wants: c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause) -- a row that adds an offer to another row's augment
p13043:augment1.why: an aspect daily whose Augment 1 is bought when some other at-will is augmented, not when this row is used

p13051:augment1.wants: Position.squares holding a second, separate square for one creature
p13051:augment1.why: both augments are built on occupying two squares at once, which the unaugmented row already had to drop

p13051:augment2.wants: Position.squares holding a second, separate square for one creature
p13051:augment2.why: Augment 2 puts the double five squares away and is the same gap

p13053:augment1.wants: a compendium ref for the class-feature step power, as dsl.REGISTRY has none for it
p13053:augment1.why: both augments only lengthen the rider on that feature, which the unaugmented row already had to drop for the same reason

p13053:augment2.wants: a compendium ref for the class-feature step power, as dsl.REGISTRY has none for it
p13053:augment2.why: Augment 2's teleport is that same rider; its 2[W] is not written alone because half a clause is worse than none

p13311:augment1.wants: a third command on dsl.Summon, beyond its standard and opportunity attacks
p13311:augment1.why: Augment 1 gives the servant an opportunity action that makes a Heal check on a dying ally, and Summon declares two attack lines and nothing else

p13318:augment1.wants: c.penalty_in(zone, what, value) -- a modifier scoped to a zone or an aura, as c.resist_in and c.cover_in already are
p13318:augment1.why: enemies take -2 to attack rolls while adjacent to the target, and nothing scopes an attack modifier to a footprint

p13325:augment1.wants: a rider on dsl.Summon's attack line, so a summoned creature's grab can be applied
p13325:augment1.why: the penalty is to escaping a grab the summon never applies, so the clause could never come up

p13783:augment1.wants: SkillCheck.purpose, so a bonus can be gated to checks made to find hidden creatures
p13783:augment1.why: the clause is +5 to Perception checks made for one reason, and a check carries no reason to gate on, so the bonus would apply to every Perception check the ardent makes

p2621:augment1.wants: compendium.augment_body -- the imported page prints only a Special: line between the two Augment headings, so Augment 1 has no Hit line to write and no symbol can ever arrive
p2621:augment1.why: the imported entry has no Hit line under its Augment 1 heading -- only the Special that belongs to the whole power sits between the two headings -- so there is no clause to write

p2622:augment1.wants: a compendium ref for the class-feature attack, as dsl.REGISTRY has none for it
p2622:augment1.why: Augment 1 pays extra damage on a later use of the battlemind's own feature attack, which the spec names in prose with no id beside it

p8240:augment1.wants: c.strip_resistance(dtype, on=) -- taking a standing resistance away, which c.resist only adds
p8240:augment1.why: the clause fixes the vulnerability at 5 and then strips the target's psychic resistance; the second half has no method, and writing the first alone would be half a clause
